bull_bear.body:
- Well-established, high recall value brand with a 60-year legacy in the hospitality, travel and tourism ecosystem; Trust, Service Standards and Climate and Resilience are described as the hallmark of its brand value
- Zero debt, profit-making Mini Ratna with the highest CARE A1+ rating for short term banking facilities, and generating cash surplus from operations, putting it in a strong position to undertake new growth-oriented projects
- Well trained and empowered pool of highly skilled and experienced human capital plus physical-social infrastructure that maintains benchmark service standards
- Trusted, reliable and preferred provider for Government institutional hospitality — Padma Awardees, UPSC, NFDC, Central Ministries, PSUs, State Bhawans and Embassies
- World-class banquet and convention infrastructure at The Ashok underpinning leadership in India's growing MICE sector
- Valuable estate/land portfolio available for monetisation and commercial development
- Diversified SBU structure spanning hotels, events, travel, duty free, engineering consultancy and hospitality education
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on Government clients — BRSR material issues identify 'Major Dependencies on Govt. Clients' as a risk because the maximum share of clients are Government/Ministries/PSUs; efforts are being made to fetch private business also, and the SWOT states ITDC has to diversify its portfolio and outreach beyond its high dependence on the Government Sector. Financial implication disclosed as negative, not assessed.
- Ongoing hotel disinvestment and loss of chain advantage — Management calls the persistent unpredictability from the ongoing disinvestment process of hotels, with its consequential impact on human resources, a major challenge in need of resolution. BRSR separately lists 'Loss of chain advantage' as a risk due to the Government's disinvestment/divestment policy for hotels and closure of ATT offices outside Delhi; all four subsidiaries are under disinvestment, two with closed hotel operations and one incomplete project.
- Cyclical and shock-sensitive demand for tourism — Management states tourism is a sensitive product affected by general economic conditions such as global recession and inflation, socio-political risk domestically and internationally, and travel advisories from foreign countries. The recent geo-political crisis in Hormuz is cited as exposing vulnerabilities in the travel, tourism and hospitality sector, and FY26 is described as a year book-ended by geo political instability.
- Competition from international hotel chains and increased outbound travel — Explicitly listed under Risk and Concerns; compounded by an industry shift from owner-owned hotels to developer-operator and franchisee models, rising deal signings and new brands across segments, and new hotels with ultra-modern facilities on the anvil, against ITDC's ageing properties.
- Ageing properties requiring continuous remedial capex — The SWOT weakness section concedes issues relating to ITDC's ageing properties are 'at best remedial'; renovation and refurbishment is under execution at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat and capex funds are being used for statutory fire and safety compliance to service high-end clientele.
- IT and technology under-investment — Management states a substantial investment is required in identifying, upgrading and up-scaling IT infrastructure to mimic technological changes in the world and in the sector for personalised experiences; travellers increasingly decide via platforms, aggregators and payment gateways, and BRSR flags digital transformation of travel services as an opportunity requiring adoption of digital processes.
- Human capital skill gap and domain-functionary shortage — The SWOT notes human capital may be in need of up-skilling and re-learning to remain relevant, particularly in crisis communication, Artificial Intelligence and Cyber Security and Investigations; management flags that the quantum and quality of skilled professionals and increasing dependency on technology and AI requires serious assessment and re-alignment. Need-based recruitment has been initiated to mitigate the shortage of domain-specific functionaries; against 34 vacancies advertised in FY 2025-26, 11 candidates joined.
- Audit qualifications and unresolved receivable/compliance matters — Statutory auditors qualified the accounts on MSMED Act compliance (unable to determine delay, interest liability and compliance), on licence fees not invoiced at Ashok Hotel, Samrat Hotel and Taj Restaurant which leaves sale of services and trade receivables understated and remains under board consideration, and on the erstwhile General Sales Agent arrangement of Ashok Travels & Tours where the amount receivable exceeds the security held on 'HOLD', leaving a deficit.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: ITDC operates hotels and catering units, an event-management business, a travel and tour agency, duty-free retail, engineering/consultancy and a hospitality institute, largely serving government ministries, PSUs, embassies, corporates and individual travellers. Hotels & Catering accounts for 61% of turnover and Event Management for 31%. Its clients are Individuals, Corporates, State Governments, Central Government, PSUs, Ministries/Government Departments, FIs, Business Travellers, Groups and MICE.

- **Hotels & Catering:** The Ashok, New Delhi, Hotel Samrat, New Delhi, Hotel Kalinga Ashok, Bhubaneswar, Taj Restaurant, Agra, Ashok Pondicherry Beach Resort, Parliament House Catering Unit, New Delhi, Hyderabad House, New Delhi, Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, Western Court Canteens, New Delhi, ITDC Gift Card

outlook.body:
- Re-imagine the corporate Vision as part of VikshitBharat@2047 in light of a post-pandemic, data-digital and AI-led decision-making environment
- Strengthen and enlarge the potential SBUs through SBU-specific strategy and shift the customer base from B2G towards B2C and B2B, reducing high dependence on the Government sector
- Monetise and optimise the estate portfolio — preparatory activities for an Expression of Interest for leasing and development of the Nairana Property, and examination of strategic options for the Gwalior Property
- Carve out value from available spaces at existing properties: the renovated Samrat swimming pool, 50,000 sq. meters of new commercial spaces at Airawat Aoron and Aishwarya Lawns for weddings, banquets, flea markets, music in the gardens, exhibitions and melas, and the upcoming Gardenia Restaurant at Samrat
- Digital modernisation: launch of the ITDC Online Booking Portal for Government Ministries, PSUs and Defence/Paramilitary forces offering a single integrated portal for flights, hotels, transport, conferences and events
- Reposition Ashok Travels & Tours as a 'One-Stop Shop' for the travel ecosystem — bespoke tour packages, visa/passport and apostille services, concierge, ticketing with secure payment gateways, transport and hotel accommodation
- Build a data and analytics capability through the new Ashok Business Insights Division (approved by the Board on 12.08.2025) as a dedicated Data Analytics Centre supporting planning, benchmarking, market price discovery and strategic assessment
- Expand heritage and cultural tourism infrastructure, including state-of-the-art Sound & Light shows using projection mapping, laser technology and immersive systems at Leh, Purana Qila, Bundi, Sarkhej Roza and Udayagiri & Khandigiri
- Upgrade and modernise hotel infrastructure at The Ashok, Hotel Samrat and Hotel Kalinga Ashok, using capex funds for renovations and statutory fire and safety compliance in order to service high-end clientele
- Strengthen banquet and MICE business, license out vacant spaces and improve operational efficiencies across hotels and catering units
- Position IHM Ashok as a Centre of Excellence in hospitality service education and build capacity, including structured training of tribal homestay operators under an MoU with the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
- Explore collaboration with the Delhi Government, NDMC, DDA, Department of Capital Development and NBCC to develop Delhi as a cultural and creative space using ITDC's Strategic Business Units
- Adopt a digital-first marketing approach using data analytics, influencer ecosystems and OTA alliances (MakeMyTrip, ClearTrip, Booking.com, Goibibo, Expedia) to drive MICE, wedding and SBU demand
- Expand adoption of renewable energy technologies, wastewater recycling and waste management, and integrate sustainability into all major infrastructure and asset development initiatives
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: ITDC's expansion in FY 2025-26 is renovation- and monetisation-led rather than greenfield. Infrastructure upgrade work has been undertaken at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat, New Delhi, and Hotel Kalinga Ashok, Bhubaneswar, with extensive renovation and refurbishment of guest rooms, toilets, common areas and associated facilities presently under execution at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat. At Hotel Kalinga Ashok, works covering renovation of guest room toilets, installation of energy-efficient five-star inverter air-conditioning systems, upgrading of electrical and mechanical infrastructure and improvement of power backup systems were awarded and completed during the year; a 13-passenger guest lift has been completed and the hotel is now fire-compliant following completion of fire safety works. At the Delhi properties, the Samrat swimming pool has been renovated, 50,000 sq. meters of new commercial spaces have been added at Airawat Aoron and Aishwarya Lawns for weddings, banquets, flea markets, music in the gardens, exhibitions and melas, and a Gardenia Restaurant at Samrat is upcoming; management describes this as carving out value from available spaces to create more commercial opportunities, with capex funds also used for renovations and statutory fire and safety compliance to service high-end clientele. On the estate side, the Engineering & Estate Division is undertaking preparatory activities for inviting an Expression of Interest for leasing and development of the Nairana Property, while strategic options for the Gwalior Property are being examined under the Corporation's asset optimisation objectives. In heritage tourism infrastructure the Division is executing the 'Development of Spiritual Circuit: Sivagiri' project and a teaser series of state-of-the-art Sound & Light shows has been inaugurated at Leh, Purana Qila, Bundi, Sarkhej Roza and Udayagiri & Khandigiri using projection mapping, laser technology, synchronized audio and high-resolution immersive systems. Duty-free footprint stood at 14 shops in operation at seaports and one at Visakhapatnam Airport during 2025-26. Management also flags that substantial investment is required in identifying, upgrading and up-scaling IT infrastructure. Environment-related capital work includes Sewage Treatment Plants (1 MLD at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat; 30 KLD STP/ETP at Hotel Kalinga Ashok), rainwater harvesting, Organic Waste Converters at The Ashok and Samrat, revamping of STPs at the Pondicherry hotel, and the intent to further expand renewable energy adoption and wastewater recycling.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's domestic tourism landscape continues to witness robust demand across all segments
- The wedding industry is poised for sustained growth, driven by urbanisation, rising disposable incomes and evolving consumer aspirations
- India is emerging as a compelling MICE destination for both domestic and inbound tourism markets
- Tourism currently contributes 5% to GDP and is expected to double as India moves from a USD 4.187 trillion economy towards a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047; the Services Sector contributes 54% to GDP and ITDC expects to remain equally if not more relevant
- Government policy thrust on Wed in India, Meet in India, Medical Value and Heal in India tourism, immersive sound and light experiences, music concerts, a festival and event-based economy and recreational/rejuvenation tourism is expected to unlock new avenues for ITDC
- The post-pandemic traveller increasingly makes travel and hospitality decisions aided by data insights and technology, using platforms, networks, aggregators and payment gateways
- The hotel industry is shifting from owner-owned hotels to developer-operator and franchisee models, with rising deal signings, listings and new brands across segments; gourmet and curated experiences are becoming fundamental to hospitality
- Domestic demand resilience is the buffer against geo-political shocks — the Hormuz crisis exposed vulnerabilities in the travel, tourism and hospitality sector
- Hotels Division turnover was `339.70 crore in FY 2025-26, closely aligned with the previous year's `338.17 crore, reflecting consistent performance and stability in a highly competitive market and a year book-ended by geo political instability
- The ITDC Gift Card, available in multiple denominations and redeemable for room stays and F&B, is an additional revenue stream supporting festive gifting, employee rewards and corporate engagements
- ITDC is a significant contributor to India's ever-expanding tourism infrastructure, which offers continuing commercial opportunities
- Persistent unpredictability from the ongoing hotel disinvestment process, with its consequential impact on human resources, remains a major challenge in need of resolution

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India Tourism Development Corporation is a listed Mini Ratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Tourism that positions itself as a 'one stop solution provider' in hospitality, travel and tourism, with a 60-year legacy brand and five Strategic Business Units.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ITDC operates hotels and catering units, an event-management business, a travel and tour agency, duty-free retail, engineering/consultancy and a hospitality institute, largely serving government ministries, PSUs, embassies, corporates and individual travellers. Hotels & Catering accounts for 61% of turnover and Event Management for 31%. Its clients are Individuals, Corporates, State Governments, Central Government, PSUs, Ministries/Government Departments, FIs, Business Travellers, Groups and MICE.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Pondicherry Ashok Hotel Corporation Limited — subsidiary: 51% held by ITDC; hotel operating subsidiary, currently under the disinvestment process; does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives; acquired 16/6/1986
- Ranchi Ashok Bihar Hotel Corporation Limited — subsidiary: 51% held by ITDC; operations of the hotel are closed and the company is under the disinvestment process; acquired 23/7/1983
- Punjab Ashok Hotel Company Limited — subsidiary: 51% held by ITDC; hotel project is incomplete, the company is yet to commence operations and is under the disinvestment process; acquired 11/11/1998
- Utkal Ashok Hotel Corporation Limited — subsidiary: 91.54% held by ITDC; operations of the hotel have been closed since 2005 and the company is under the disinvestment process; acquired 2/11/1983
- Ministry of Tourism, Government of India — related party: Administrative ministry of ITDC as a CPSE; appoints all directors, signs an annual MoU with the Corporation containing key performance parameters, and evaluates board performance
- M/s MSIL — related party: Counterparty to a sub-lease of the workshop-cum-depot at Plot No. C-119, Naraina Industrial Area, Phase-I, New Delhi; subject of long-running eviction and damages proceedings under the Public Premises Act, 1971; MSIL vacated the premises on December 4, 2024

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Hotels & Catering:** The Ashok, New Delhi, Hotel Samrat, New Delhi, Hotel Kalinga Ashok, Bhubaneswar, Taj Restaurant, Agra, Ashok Pondicherry Beach Resort, Parliament House Catering Unit, New Delhi, Hyderabad House, New Delhi, Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, Western Court Canteens, New Delhi, ITDC Gift Card
- **Event Management:** Ashok Events (Professional Conference Organiser; Bharat Parv, Bharat Tribes Fest, International Tourism Mart)
- **Travel & Tours:** Ashok Travels & Tours (bespoke tour packages, visa and passport services, apostille, concierge, ticketing platform, transport), ITDC Online Booking Portal for Government Ministries, PSUs and Defence/Paramilitary forces
- **Duty Free Retail:** Ashok International Trade Division duty free shops
- **Engineering & Consultancy:** Engineering & Estate Division, Ashok Consultancy & Engineering Services (ACES), Sound & Light Shows (Leh, Purana Qila, Bundi, Sarkhej Roza, Udayagiri & Khandagiri)
- **Hospitality Education:** IHM Ashok (formerly The Ashok Institute of Hospitality and Tourism Management)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:

- Government, Ministries, PSUs, State Bhawans and Embassies (B2G institutional hospitality)
- MICE — conferences, exhibitions and conventions
- Weddings and social events

certifications.body:

- CARE A1+ rating for short term banking facilities (highest rating)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's domestic tourism landscape continues to witness robust demand across all segments
- The wedding industry is poised for sustained growth, driven by urbanisation, rising disposable incomes and evolving consumer aspirations
- India is emerging as a compelling MICE destination for both domestic and inbound tourism markets
- Tourism currently contributes 5% to GDP and is expected to double as India moves from a USD 4.187 trillion economy towards a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047; the Services Sector contributes 54% to GDP and ITDC expects to remain equally if not more relevant
- Government policy thrust on Wed in India, Meet in India, Medical Value and Heal in India tourism, immersive sound and light experiences, music concerts, a festival and event-based economy and recreational/rejuvenation tourism is expected to unlock new avenues for ITDC
- The post-pandemic traveller increasingly makes travel and hospitality decisions aided by data insights and technology, using platforms, networks, aggregators and payment gateways
- The hotel industry is shifting from owner-owned hotels to developer-operator and franchisee models, with rising deal signings, listings and new brands across segments; gourmet and curated experiences are becoming fundamental to hospitality
- Domestic demand resilience is the buffer against geo-political shocks — the Hormuz crisis exposed vulnerabilities in the travel, tourism and hospitality sector
- Hotels Division turnover was `339.70 crore in FY 2025-26, closely aligned with the previous year's `338.17 crore, reflecting consistent performance and stability in a highly competitive market and a year book-ended by geo political instability
- The ITDC Gift Card, available in multiple denominations and redeemable for room stays and F&B, is an additional revenue stream supporting festive gifting, employee rewards and corporate engagements
- ITDC is a significant contributor to India's ever-expanding tourism infrastructure, which offers continuing commercial opportunities
- Persistent unpredictability from the ongoing hotel disinvestment process, with its consequential impact on human resources, remains a major challenge in need of resolution

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Re-imagine the corporate Vision as part of VikshitBharat@2047 in light of a post-pandemic, data-digital and AI-led decision-making environment
- Strengthen and enlarge the potential SBUs through SBU-specific strategy and shift the customer base from B2G towards B2C and B2B, reducing high dependence on the Government sector
- Monetise and optimise the estate portfolio — preparatory activities for an Expression of Interest for leasing and development of the Nairana Property, and examination of strategic options for the Gwalior Property
- Carve out value from available spaces at existing properties: the renovated Samrat swimming pool, 50,000 sq. meters of new commercial spaces at Airawat Aoron and Aishwarya Lawns for weddings, banquets, flea markets, music in the gardens, exhibitions and melas, and the upcoming Gardenia Restaurant at Samrat
- Digital modernisation: launch of the ITDC Online Booking Portal for Government Ministries, PSUs and Defence/Paramilitary forces offering a single integrated portal for flights, hotels, transport, conferences and events
- Reposition Ashok Travels & Tours as a 'One-Stop Shop' for the travel ecosystem — bespoke tour packages, visa/passport and apostille services, concierge, ticketing with secure payment gateways, transport and hotel accommodation
- Build a data and analytics capability through the new Ashok Business Insights Division (approved by the Board on 12.08.2025) as a dedicated Data Analytics Centre supporting planning, benchmarking, market price discovery and strategic assessment
- Expand heritage and cultural tourism infrastructure, including state-of-the-art Sound & Light shows using projection mapping, laser technology and immersive systems at Leh, Purana Qila, Bundi, Sarkhej Roza and Udayagiri & Khandigiri
- Upgrade and modernise hotel infrastructure at The Ashok, Hotel Samrat and Hotel Kalinga Ashok, using capex funds for renovations and statutory fire and safety compliance in order to service high-end clientele
- Strengthen banquet and MICE business, license out vacant spaces and improve operational efficiencies across hotels and catering units
- Position IHM Ashok as a Centre of Excellence in hospitality service education and build capacity, including structured training of tribal homestay operators under an MoU with the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
- Explore collaboration with the Delhi Government, NDMC, DDA, Department of Capital Development and NBCC to develop Delhi as a cultural and creative space using ITDC's Strategic Business Units
- Adopt a digital-first marketing approach using data analytics, influencer ecosystems and OTA alliances (MakeMyTrip, ClearTrip, Booking.com, Goibibo, Expedia) to drive MICE, wedding and SBU demand
- Expand adoption of renewable energy technologies, wastewater recycling and waste management, and integrate sustainability into all major infrastructure and asset development initiatives

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: ITDC's expansion in FY 2025-26 is renovation- and monetisation-led rather than greenfield. Infrastructure upgrade work has been undertaken at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat, New Delhi, and Hotel Kalinga Ashok, Bhubaneswar, with extensive renovation and refurbishment of guest rooms, toilets, common areas and associated facilities presently under execution at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat. At Hotel Kalinga Ashok, works covering renovation of guest room toilets, installation of energy-efficient five-star inverter air-conditioning systems, upgrading of electrical and mechanical infrastructure and improvement of power backup systems were awarded and completed during the year; a 13-passenger guest lift has been completed and the hotel is now fire-compliant following completion of fire safety works. At the Delhi properties, the Samrat swimming pool has been renovated, 50,000 sq. meters of new commercial spaces have been added at Airawat Aoron and Aishwarya Lawns for weddings, banquets, flea markets, music in the gardens, exhibitions and melas, and a Gardenia Restaurant at Samrat is upcoming; management describes this as carving out value from available spaces to create more commercial opportunities, with capex funds also used for renovations and statutory fire and safety compliance to service high-end clientele. On the estate side, the Engineering & Estate Division is undertaking preparatory activities for inviting an Expression of Interest for leasing and development of the Nairana Property, while strategic options for the Gwalior Property are being examined under the Corporation's asset optimisation objectives. In heritage tourism infrastructure the Division is executing the 'Development of Spiritual Circuit: Sivagiri' project and a teaser series of state-of-the-art Sound & Light shows has been inaugurated at Leh, Purana Qila, Bundi, Sarkhej Roza and Udayagiri & Khandigiri using projection mapping, laser technology, synchronized audio and high-resolution immersive systems. Duty-free footprint stood at 14 shops in operation at seaports and one at Visakhapatnam Airport during 2025-26. Management also flags that substantial investment is required in identifying, upgrading and up-scaling IT infrastructure. Environment-related capital work includes Sewage Treatment Plants (1 MLD at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat; 30 KLD STP/ETP at Hotel Kalinga Ashok), rainwater harvesting, Organic Waste Converters at The Ashok and Samrat, revamping of STPs at the Pondicherry hotel, and the intent to further expand renewable energy adoption and wastewater recycling.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Well-established, high recall value brand with a 60-year legacy in the hospitality, travel and tourism ecosystem; Trust, Service Standards and Climate and Resilience are described as the hallmark of its brand value
- Zero debt, profit-making Mini Ratna with the highest CARE A1+ rating for short term banking facilities, and generating cash surplus from operations, putting it in a strong position to undertake new growth-oriented projects
- Well trained and empowered pool of highly skilled and experienced human capital plus physical-social infrastructure that maintains benchmark service standards
- Trusted, reliable and preferred provider for Government institutional hospitality — Padma Awardees, UPSC, NFDC, Central Ministries, PSUs, State Bhawans and Embassies
- World-class banquet and convention infrastructure at The Ashok underpinning leadership in India's growing MICE sector
- Valuable estate/land portfolio available for monetisation and commercial development
- Diversified SBU structure spanning hotels, events, travel, duty free, engineering consultancy and hospitality education

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on Government clients — BRSR material issues identify 'Major Dependencies on Govt. Clients' as a risk because the maximum share of clients are Government/Ministries/PSUs; efforts are being made to fetch private business also, and the SWOT states ITDC has to diversify its portfolio and outreach beyond its high dependence on the Government Sector. Financial implication disclosed as negative, not assessed.
- Ongoing hotel disinvestment and loss of chain advantage — Management calls the persistent unpredictability from the ongoing disinvestment process of hotels, with its consequential impact on human resources, a major challenge in need of resolution. BRSR separately lists 'Loss of chain advantage' as a risk due to the Government's disinvestment/divestment policy for hotels and closure of ATT offices outside Delhi; all four subsidiaries are under disinvestment, two with closed hotel operations and one incomplete project.
- Cyclical and shock-sensitive demand for tourism — Management states tourism is a sensitive product affected by general economic conditions such as global recession and inflation, socio-political risk domestically and internationally, and travel advisories from foreign countries. The recent geo-political crisis in Hormuz is cited as exposing vulnerabilities in the travel, tourism and hospitality sector, and FY26 is described as a year book-ended by geo political instability.
- Competition from international hotel chains and increased outbound travel — Explicitly listed under Risk and Concerns; compounded by an industry shift from owner-owned hotels to developer-operator and franchisee models, rising deal signings and new brands across segments, and new hotels with ultra-modern facilities on the anvil, against ITDC's ageing properties.
- Ageing properties requiring continuous remedial capex — The SWOT weakness section concedes issues relating to ITDC's ageing properties are 'at best remedial'; renovation and refurbishment is under execution at The Ashok and Hotel Samrat and capex funds are being used for statutory fire and safety compliance to service high-end clientele.
- IT and technology under-investment — Management states a substantial investment is required in identifying, upgrading and up-scaling IT infrastructure to mimic technological changes in the world and in the sector for personalised experiences; travellers increasingly decide via platforms, aggregators and payment gateways, and BRSR flags digital transformation of travel services as an opportunity requiring adoption of digital processes.
- Human capital skill gap and domain-functionary shortage — The SWOT notes human capital may be in need of up-skilling and re-learning to remain relevant, particularly in crisis communication, Artificial Intelligence and Cyber Security and Investigations; management flags that the quantum and quality of skilled professionals and increasing dependency on technology and AI requires serious assessment and re-alignment. Need-based recruitment has been initiated to mitigate the shortage of domain-specific functionaries; against 34 vacancies advertised in FY 2025-26, 11 candidates joined.
- Audit qualifications and unresolved receivable/compliance matters — Statutory auditors qualified the accounts on MSMED Act compliance (unable to determine delay, interest liability and compliance), on licence fees not invoiced at Ashok Hotel, Samrat Hotel and Taj Restaurant which leaves sale of services and trade receivables understated and remains under board consideration, and on the erstwhile General Sales Agent arrangement of Ashok Travels & Tours where the amount receivable exceeds the security held on 'HOLD', leaving a deficit.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
